never ask a child to rate or grade anything in words - FPS-R has severity, and Tu 2025's 'markedly reduced' is an examiner's grading

already banned globally; restated because this packet's differential contains three orthopaedic emergencies and the temptation to signal urgency is real

imperative mood -- the packet's highest-risk ruling (decision 5) and the only one the old keyword list could not catch. "Run around and tell me if it hurts" is an examination delegated to a child; "does it hurt more when you run around?" asks about a pattern they already noticed
\b(hot|warm|boiling|burning up|overheated)\b

item 11 must anchor on waking up, not on feeling hot -- "do you get hot in the night?" lands on the feels-feverish fact, which decision 11 calls actively harmful because row 1 will own that fact across four packets

clinical register for item 8, ruled out in decision 1. The adjective "stiff" is the app's own shipped vocabulary and stays legal; the noun and "restricted" are a clinician describing a child

the body-weight ban is a ban on the CONCEPT, not on the word "weight" -- decision 1 gives "are you a big boy?" as the worked example and the old regex matched none of it
